newsitem.title: USA: Kids Mart closes stores, future uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Kids Mart closes stores, future uncertain.

text.p: Kids Mart Inc said Tuesday it had closed 97 stores and cut staff, and it said this would result in an estimated third-quarter operations charge of about $5.4 million.
The company said there are no assurances it will become more profitable, and auditors question its ability to continue as a going concern.
Kids Mart said it anticipates it may be in violation of certain loan covenants under its credit agreement.
It is in the midst of negotiations with its principal lender to try to waive or amend those covenants.
Kids Mart said it had decided to close the stores in an effort to reverse substantial losses and cash-flow constraints it has been experiencing over the past 12 months.
For the eight months ended January 27 and the six months ended July 27, net losses were $5.7 million and $8.6 million, respectively.
The company said another 10 stores may be closed.
Kids Mart said it is seeking immediate interim financing to buy inventory for the upcoming holiday sales season.
It said failure to achieve adequate sales levels during the holiday season would have a material effect on its business.
The company has held discussions with financial advisers and potential investors, seeking interim financing through short-term subordinated debt, equity investment or debt restructuring.
So far, it has reached no definitive agreements, and it said there are no assurances it will receive interim financing or that such financing will arrive in a timely fashion.
The company also said there are no assurances that if it received interim financing, it would be enough to sustain it "for a reasonable period of time."
Kids Mart has raised about $900,000 through a sale/leaseback transaction and conversion of a vendor account payable to 433,333 shares of the company's common stock.
This vendor was also granted the right to have its nominee installed as a member of the company's board of directors.
Kids Mart is a chain of children's specialty apparel stores. After the store closures, the company will operate about 182 stores in 18 states under the names Little Folks and Kids Mart.
